data.turoyo: Gədmḥammina ruḥan w, xəd alo w d u=ʕulmo, w mibarxina u=aṯto w u=gawro na. Haṯe ste kobaʕla mede?
data.translation: Wir werden uns baden und werden uns verheiraten, wie es bei Gott und der weiten Sitte ist, und wir sind Mann und Frau. Braucht es dazu noch viele Worte?

rationale: Thin Infectum cell: overt ruḥan reflexive object with gəd- contrasts with both zero-object and reciprocal uses in the inherited example.

after: baden im Badhaus, sich baden; jmndn. baden;
rationale: The existing Imperativ already orders bathing another person, and the existing Infectum has reciprocal ḥḏoḏe. State the transitive meaning omitted by the self-bathing-only gloss.

summary: All five tokens retain stem II. Zero-object self-bathing, overt ruḥan self-bathing and reciprocal ḥḏoḏe occur with active II morphology.
The 77/193 Imperativ has a suffixed third-person patient and clearly directs servants to bathe someone else. The gloss change repairs an already exemplified valency, not a new numbered sense.
The two 88/69 tokens are already together in one quotation. Only the distinct overt-reflexive passage at 88/252 is added.
No ritual or marriage-specific bathing sense is inferred from the subsequent marriage in 88/252; the bathing action remains ordinary. Active self-bathing does not justify a Detransitive section.
